newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas opens up on well blowout, then mixed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas opens up on well blowout, then mixed.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures opened higher, then pared gains Tuesday morning, as early buying on news of a Louisiana gas well blowout gave way to technical selling at resistance, market sources said.
At 1215 EDT, July climbed 0.8 cent to $2.155 per million British thermal units, while August was up the same at $2.165. Other deferreds were narrowly mixed.

"The market got hyped early on the (gas well) explosion, but it couldn's hold. I don't think there are a whole lot of shorts left to cover and we could test lower numbers," said one East Coast trader.
Traders said news of a well blowout near Morgan City, Louisiana, helped trigger some early buying, but most agreed the incident had no long-term market impact. The well is flowing about 20 mmcfd.
Technical traders said the market remained range-bound, with little on the horizon to encourage either bulls or bears.
They still pegged July resistance at $2.21 and then at $2.25 and $2.37. Support was seen at last week's low of $2.055 and then at $2.

With mostly seasonal U.S. temperatures forecast for this week, few traders expected a significant rally, but they noted some forecasts were calling for hotter weather later this week and next, a factor which could underpin prices near-term.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's AGA stock report range from 78 to 110 bcf versus a gain of 87 bcf a year ago.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas was talked little changed in the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes gained a couple of cents to near the $2.05 level. New York city gate gas was flat on the day in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
NYMEX said 13,523 contracts traded at 1145 EDT. Hub open interest on June 16 rose 1,381 contracts to 199,774.

On KCBT, July firmed by one-half cent to $2.015, while deferreds were steady to one cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.3 cent to 14.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on June 16 rose six lots to 2,670.
